# SSH-014: Authorized keys are strong and not stale

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

DSA keys and RSA keys under 2048 bits are weak enough to retire. Keys in root's authorized_keys while root login is off are leftovers that start working again the day someone relaxes PermitRootLogin. Only the key type and size are kept, never the key or its comment.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ssh-keygen -lf ~USER/.ssh/authorized_keys
```

## How to fix it

Replace weak keys with ed25519 (ssh-keygen -t ed25519) and remove root's authorized keys once nothing logs in as root.

Run `stackward explain SSH-014` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
